newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea '97 GDP seen growing 6.4 pct - central bank.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea '97 GDP seen growing 6.4 pct - central bank.

text.p: South Korea's central bank said on Friday it expected the country's gross domestic product (GDP) to grow a real 6.4 percent in 1997 against this year's estimated growth of 6.9 percent.
The Bank of Korea said in a statement the GDP was projected to rise a real 6.9 percent in 1996, against a 9.0 percent growth last year.
"We plan to put more emphasis on stability than growth next year to curb the widening current account deficit," Bank of Korea's assitant governor Kim Young-dae told Reuters.
"As a result, we see the GDP growth at 6.4 percent. But we may have to accept a lower growth if we want to quickly improve the structural weakness of the economy," he added.
The central bank said on Thursday the GDP grew a real 6.4 percent in the third quarter of this year, down from a 9.8 percent rise a year earlier.
Lee Kang-nam, director of the bank's statistics division, told reporters that the economy slowed due largely to a slowdown in exports and capital investment.
The bank also forecast the nation's current account deficit at about $18 billion in 1997, down from an estimated $22 billion for this year.
"Our exports are likely to pick up in 1997 in line with the world's economic recovery," Kim Kim.
Kim said the current account deficit could fall to $13 billion next year if the GDP growth was brought down to 5.5 percent.
The central bank said the consumer price index, South Korea's leading inflation indicator, would rise by 4.7 percent in 1997, compared with an estimated 4.5 percent this year.
The consumer inflation rose 4.7 percent in 1995.
The bank statement said the unemployment rate was seen rising to 2.2 percent next year from this year's two percent.
